title: Preserve portable raw objects through scoped conditional mutations and catalog repair
description:
As an application embedding Kanbus, I want a generic scoped store with conditional idempotent mutations so that local and cloud apps preserve raw records and history without cross-tenant access. Cross-project initiative: kbs-3df9cc93-530f-4614-98a0-aa175012c1b5.

Feature: Scoped durable storage
Scenario: Lossless conditional mutation
Given a raw JSON record and history in one account and project
When a mutation uses the current revision and a unique command identifier
Then raw content and history round-trip exactly and the revision advances once
Scenario: Retry and stale mutation
Given a committed command
When the identical command is retried or a stale revision is submitted
Then the retry returns its original result and the stale mutation changes nothing
Scenario: Private oversized payload
Given a payload exceeding the inline limit
When it is written through the cloud adapter
Then immutable private S3 content is staged before conditional publication and a failed upload or mutation leaves the visible record intact
Scenario: Tenant isolation
Given the same issue identifier in different projects
When a generic field query or mutation executes within one scope
Then records in other scopes are inaccessible

Implementation uses a Rust-only workspace crate consistent with the existing Amplify/AppSync crates. No CRM-specific API, persistent AWS provisioning, production deploy, or publication in this task.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Acceptance correction from Ryan: Given ordinary Kanbus project files including unknown JSON fields and whitespace, When files are stored locally or under the S3 namespace, Then their bytes and relative paths are identical and export/import is a direct folder copy. Given concurrent mutations, When expected opaque revision differs, Then the issue remains unchanged. Given issue publication succeeds but an event or card projection fails, When the same operation is retried, Then a separate durable journal repairs remaining publication without rewriting a newer issue. S3 contains all canonical issue/history/config/attachment bytes at normal paths; DynamoDB contains only scoped card metadata and pointers. No inline payload, size threshold, content-addressed canonical layout, or multi-object atomicity claim. Parent initiative kbs-3df9cc93-530f-4614-98a0-aa175012c1b5.
